title: Ken Thompson's 'Reflections on Trusting Trust' (1984)
explainer: In his 1983 Turing Award lecture, published in 1984, Ken Thompson showed how a compiler could be secretly modified to plant a backdoor in every program it compiles - including a freshly recompiled copy of itself - leaving no trace in any source code you could read. It's the founding argument for software supply-chain distrust: you're trusting not just the code you can see, but every tool and artifact used to build it. Image-hygiene practices like pinning digests, scanning layers, and verifying build provenance exist because a container image is a compiled, opaque artifact whose contents you usually didn't build yourself.
